content: 1. The sixth edition of the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on the use of pesticides for controlling vectors and pests of public health significance was published in Geneva. 2. WHO has released a practitioner’s guide on the application of insecticides through space spraying for vector and public health pest control. 3. The second edition of the WHO manual on indoor residual spraying, which provides guidance on the application of residual sprays for vector control, was published in Geneva. 4. The International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management serves as a key reference for pesticide use and regulation. 5. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) published guidelines in 2001 on the minimum requirements for agricultural pesticide application equipment. 6. FAO also released standards and testing procedures for agricultural pesticide application equipment in 2001. 7. FAO guidelines from 2001 outline procedures for the registration, certification, and testing of new pesticide application equipment. 8. FAO published guidelines in 2001 on organizing schemes for testing and certifying agricultural pesticide sprayers in use. 9. WHO revised its specification guidelines for vector control equipment in 2010. 10. FAO released guidelines in 2001 on organizing and operating training schemes and certification procedures for pesticide application equipment operators. 11. FAO published guidelines on the prevention and management of pesticide resistance. 12. FAO released guidelines in 2006 for evaluating the efficacy of plant protection products for registration purposes. 13. WHO has developed various guidelines for efficacy testing of public health pesticides. 14. FAO published revised guidelines in 1989 on environmental criteria for pesticide registration. 15. WHO has created generic risk assessment models for public health pesticide use. 16. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) revised its principles on good laboratory practice in 1997, which were published in 1998. 17. The Codex Alimentarius Commission published recommendations in 2003 on the submission and evaluation of pesticide residue data for estimating maximum residue levels in food and feed. 18. 19. FAO and WHO jointly published a revised manual in 2006 on the development and use of pesticide specifications. 20. FAO has developed specifications for plant protection products, which are updated periodically. 21. WHO has published specifications for public health pesticides on various dates. 22. WHO, FAO, and CIPAC released guidelines in 2005 for national laboratories on quality control of pesticide products. 23. 24. WHO and UNEP developed a resource tool for the sound management of pesticides and the diagnosis and treatment of pesticide poisoning. 25. FAO published a manual in 1996 on pesticide storage and stock control as part of its Pesticide Disposal Series. 26. FAO, UNEP, and WHO released guidelines in 1999 for managing small quantities of unwanted and obsolete pesticides. 27. FAO and WHO published guidelines in 2008 on managing empty pesticide containers. 28. The Rotterdam Convention Secretariat published a guide in 2004 on developing national laws to implement the Rotterdam Convention. 29. FAO and WHO released guidelines on pesticide registration. 30. FAO published guidelines in 2006 on compliance and enforcement of pesticide regulatory programs. 31. OECD published guidance in 2005 for country data review reports on plant protection products and their active substances. 32. OECD also released guidance in 2005 for industry data submissions on plant protection products and their active substances. 33. WHO published a recommended classification of pesticides by hazard and guidelines for classification in 2009. 34. The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) released the third revised edition of the Globally Harmonized System for the Classification and Labeling of Chemicals. 35. The International Labour Organization (ILO) published Convention No. 184 in 2001, concerning safety and health in agriculture. 36. FAO and WHO published guidelines in 2010 on pesticide advertising. 37. The United Nations released the 17th revised edition of the Model Regulations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods in 2011. 38. FAO published provisional guidelines in 1995 on preventing the accumulation of obsolete pesticide stocks. 39. The International Programme on Chemical Safety (IPCS) provides chemical safety information through its INCHEM platform. 40. FAO, UNEP, and WHO published provisional technical guidelines in 1996 on disposing of bulk quantities of obsolete pesticides in developing countries. 41. The Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and Their Disposal was adopted in 1989. 42. FAO published country-specific guidelines as part of its Pesticide Disposal Series, which remain undated. 43. FAO released a training manual in 2001 for inventory-taking of obsolete pesticides. 44. FAO published an environmental management toolkit for obsolete pesticides in 2009, consisting of two parts. 45. FAO released guidelines in 2006 on monitoring and observing the Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management. 46. The Codex Alimentarius, developed by the FAO/WHO Joint Secretariat, provides international food standards. 47. The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer, amended multiple times, was published by UNEP in 2000. 48. The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants was adopted by UNEP in 2001. 49. The ILO published Convention No. 170 on safety in the use of chemicals at work. 50. The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development was adopted by the United Nations in 1992. 51. Agenda 21, a global program of action on sustainable development, was adopted by the United Nations in 1992. 52. The Convention on Biological Diversity was adopted by UNEP in 1992. 53. The ILO published Convention No. 174 in 1993, concerning the prevention of major industrial accidents. 54. The Rome Declaration on World Food Security and the World Food Summit Plan of Action were adopted by FAO in 1996. 55. WHO published the World Health Declaration and the Health-for-All policy for the 21st century in 1998. 56. The Strategic Approach to International Chemicals Management was adopted by the International Conference on Chemicals Management in 2006.
